items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: George Carpentier, the ex-heavy weight boxing champion, had a bar next door to the Villa d'Este and he came in the club every night. He always danced at least one a night when we played and he always spoke to each one of us as he danced by.

ctx.x: So we turned a deaf ear to Freddy's plea and continued to work and it was a good thing we did because I realise not that if we had walked out we would not have been able to work any place else in Paris and may have been expelled from the country, because the owner of the Villa d'Este had the permission for us to work in France but only at the Villa d'Este until the 6-month contract that Freddy had signed was terminated. Spider, George and myself got a raise that equaled the pianists and I was considered as leader…

George Carpentier, the ex-heavy weight boxing champion, had a bar next door to the Villa d'Este and he came in the club every night. He always danced at least one a night when we played and he always spoke to each one of us as he danced by. Oscar Aleman the guitarist was a

small built fellow who was from Argentina and was very full of life. When George Carpentier spoke to Oscar, he always called him "little Monkey". George spoke English as well as I did whereas Oscar didn't know one word of English. But George had called him a little monkey so often that Oscar began to know the word and became suspicious about it being something unusual to call someone.
